description: We are a multi-disciplinary team of passionate tech trainees specializing in mobile development, web engineering, and data science. Combining predictive data modeling with responsive, user-friendly mobile and web interfaces, we bridge the gap between complex NASA datasets and practical, real-world solutions. Driven by curiosity and collaboration, our goal is to turn satellite insights into actionable tools for everyone.
summary:
ORBITALIS is an end-to-end astronaut health monitoring and analysis platform designed to safeguard crew well-being during long-duration space missions and communication blackouts.

We developed an offline-first native Android mobile application paired with a centralized mission-control web dashboard. During signal loss, the mobile app operates autonomously—allowing authenticated astronauts to log daily Complete Blood Count (CBC) biomarkers, evaluate readings immediately against personalized baselines and tolerance thresholds, and store complete records locally in SQLite. Once connectivity is restored, queued logs synchronize via REST API to a cloud backend where the web dashboard aggregates multi-modal health indicators and uses the Google Gemini API to analyze trends, flag anomalies, and generate personalized monitoring recommendations.

In deep-space environments where latency, radiation, and isolation threaten crew health, ORBITALIS guarantees zero medical data loss during blackouts while empowering flight surgeons with timely, baseline-aware clinical insights.
details:
What It Does & How It Works

ORBITALIS ("Beyond Earth. Beyond Limits. Better Health.") is an integrated astronaut health monitoring and analysis platform built for long-duration space missions where altered gravity, radiation, isolation, and communication blackouts present major medical risks. The platform bridges an offline-first mobile data collection app with a centralized AI-assisted web dashboard:

• Crew Authentication & Data Isolation: Each astronaut signs into the mobile app using a dedicated crew ID (C001–C004) secured via Firebase Authentication, keeping individual baselines and historical records isolated per crew member.

• Offline-First Daily Biomarker Logging: On the Android app, astronauts log 20 daily Complete Blood Count (CBC) biomarkers (including Hemoglobin, Hematocrit, White Blood Cell Count, Red Blood Cell Count, Platelet Count, Neutrophils, Lymphocytes, Monocytes, Eosinophils, and Basophils). Every entry is evaluated immediately on-device against that astronaut's personalized baseline and tolerance range, flagging readings as Normal, Too Low, or Too High without requiring an internet connection.

• Resilient Local Storage & REST API Sync: All daily logs are stored locally in an on-device Room (SQLite) database with sync-state tracking. When connectivity is available or restored after a blackout, pending records synchronize via REST API (sending lightweight JSON payloads containing astronautId, analyte, and value) to the central backend.

• Centralized Dashboard & AI Analysis: The web platform consolidates blood biomarkers alongside broader physiological, psychological, and environmental indicators (heart rate, blood pressure, sleep patterns, mood, stress levels, and environmental exposure). Using the Google Gemini API, the dashboard analyzes longitudinal trends against individual baselines, highlights unusual changes across mission stages, and generates personalized monitoring recommendations for medical teams.

Benefits & Intended Impact

• Zero Medical Data Loss: Ensures continuous health logging and local record persistence even during deep-space signal dropouts.

• Immediate Onboard Triage: Gives astronauts instant feedback on out-of-range biomarkers without waiting for high-latency Earth communications.

• Smarter Clinical Decisions: Replaces one-size-fits-all reference ranges with individual astronaut baselines and AI-synthesized trend insights, supporting early risk detection and safer human space exploration.

Tools, Languages & Hardware Used

• Mobile Application: Kotlin, Jetpack Compose, Material 3, MVVM Architecture, Coroutines & StateFlow, Room (SQLite), Retrofit, Gson, OkHttp, and Firebase Authentication (built in Android Studio).

• Web Frontend: React.js.

• Backend & Database: Node.js, Express.js, and MongoDB.

• AI & Data Sources: Google Gemini API and NASA open spaceflight hematology and health datasets.

• Hardware & Testing: Android smartphones (tested on Samsung Galaxy A15), development laptops, and Postman for API verification.

Creativity & Factors Considered

• Hybrid Offline-First + Cloud AI Architecture: Combines fast, deterministic baseline evaluation on the astronaut's mobile device during blackouts with deeper multi-indicator AI trend analysis on the ground/station dashboard once synced.

• Spacecraft-Ready Interface: Built with a low-glare tactical dark theme and monospace typography (Space Mono) tailored for dim cabin environments and rapid visual scanning.

• Key Engineering Factors: Our team prioritized offline reliability, strict per-astronaut authentication, compact JSON synchronization payloads for bandwidth-constrained downlinks, and personalized baseline modeling.
